rejected.finding: The Round Rock hub sits in Williamson County
rejected.reason: Neither the Round Rock city page (no occurrence of 'Williamson') nor Zipline's Austin announcement places the ETJ facility in a county. DroneXL places Round Rock the city in Williamson County (c41), and Zipline's release quotes the Williamson County judge (c31). Neither source says the hub's location is in Williamson County. The county claim for the hub itself is not carried.

rejected.finding: Round Rock routes noise complaints to Zipline
rejected.reason: The city page routes 'operational or company-specific feedback' to community@zipline.com (c13) and never mentions noise complaints. The noise-complaint wording is DroneXL's paraphrase, not the city's.

rejected.finding: Rowlett's ordinance applies in nonresidential districts (as a primary fact)
rejected.reason: The phrase is in DroneXL (c42) only. The May 20, 2025 minutes don't say it, and the ordinance attachment was not fetched. Carried only as DroneXL's report.

The minutes show 200 feet only as a P&Z recommended modification (c53). The motion adopted 'with attachment 1, as requested by the applicant', and Councilmember Reaves preferred 150 feet. The adopted distance can't be verified without the attachment or ORD-014-25 itself.

rejected.finding: Rowlett zoned for drone hubs before Zipline opened there (as a primary fact)
rejected.reason: No primary source gives a Rowlett opening date. DroneXL asserts it (c43, medium). The minutes show only that Zipline's representative said on May 20, 2025 that it had two sites in use, in Mesquite and Waxahachie (c52).

rejected.finding: DroneXL's 'council record' link as a Rowlett primary source
rejected.reason: The link goes to citizenportal.ai/articles/6225129/..., a third-party site that returned 403. It is not the council record. The real primary source is the city's own minutes at rowletttx.gov Archive.aspx?ADID=12572.

rejected.finding: Rowlett primary source via Legistar or AgendaCenter
rejected.reason: rowlett.legistar.com/Calendar.aspx showed 0 records, the Legistar web API returned HTTP 500, and rowletttx.gov/AgendaCenter returned 404. Superseded by the minutes found at rowletttx.gov/Archive.aspx?ADID=12572 (City Council minutes archive AMID=64).

rejected.finding: A hub location or delivery radius in Zipline's own Austin announcement
rejected.reason: Zipline's October 9, 2026 release names Round Rock but gives no hub address and no delivery radius. The three-mile figure comes from the city page, attributed to the company (c3), and from DroneXL (c33).

Three company figures disagree. The safety fact sheet says 'nearly 150 million commercial autonomous miles' (c25), the October 9 Austin release says 'more than 140 million miles' (c30), and DroneXL says Zipline told News 4 'more than 135 million commercial miles without a serious injury'. Each is carried only with its own source and none is a measurement. No single figure should be stated without its source.

rejected.finding: The FAA draft's Austin ceiling, comment deadline and five-metro scope as primary facts
rejected.reason: faa.gov is excluded by instruction, so the draft environmental assessment was not fetched. The figures are verified as DroneXL's relay only (c35, c36, c37), and the record item tx-2026-0186 should carry the FAA citation separately.

rejected.finding: A publication or update date for the Round Rock drone page
rejected.reason: The page has no published or last-updated date. Only an image path contains '2026/10', and that is a media upload folder, not a stated date.

rejected.finding: The Round Rock hub is at 3000 E. Palm Valley Blvd. (as a city statement)
rejected.reason: The city page gives only 'near the intersection of North Kenney Fort and Joe DiMaggio Boulevards' (c2). The street address is DroneXL's (c33), so it is carried as DroneXL's only.
